summary: The four evidence states are appropriate, but mixed legacy and qualified subject keys lack a safe comparison contract. Resolve SUBJECT-GATE-03 before further implementation planning; no adoption or quality approval.

findings.description: The proposed contract preserves legacy identity strings when evidence is omitted but compares qualified keys when it is present, without defining cross-representation or cross-namespace identity resolution. The same known person can therefore appear disjoint solely because the keys differ.
findings.evidence: Lines 15/20/32 specify qualified-key comparison, legacy fallback and source namespaces without a common identity binding or an incomparable result. The actual report boundary intersects literal sets at build_bakeoff_report.py:809. A synthetic public comparison witness retaining the same present_identities on both sides exits 5 with matching legacy keys, 0 after qualifying only one key, and 5 after aligning the keys; genuinely distinct qualified people exit 0. This exercises the existing alias boundary, not an unimplemented subject_evidence consumer.
findings.fix: Before resubmission, define an authority-backed subject identity namespace distinct from manifest/frame binding, with explicit legacy-to-qualified equivalence or a fail-closed incomparable outcome. Specify mixed and different-namespace comparisons, preserve legacy/legacy behavior and identity truth, and add public same-person negative controls plus a distinct-person positive control. Keep the unseen-person guard and require a separate protocol for any known-person mode.
